- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect downward pressure.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overcorrects in next 3–5 days; apply downward bias of 1–3% to subsequent forecasts.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 7-day average is above 30-day average, forecast should be slightly above that average to reflect reversion bias.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to be 1–2% ahead of historical pattern.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, model is likely underestimating supply/demand shock; increase forecast by 1–2% for next period.
